paper.title: No-Regret M${}^{\natural}$-Concave Function Maximization: Stochastic Bandit Algorithms and Hardness of Adversarial Full-Information Setting

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic bandit M-natural-concave function maximization (simple regret)
unmapped: Unknown reward f* is an M-natural-concave function on the integer lattice Z^d with values in [0,1]; actions are integer vectors x in dom f* with x(V) <= m (not just subsets)
learner is told the feasible set via a poly(d)-time membership oracle
settings.definition_quote: For $t = 1,\dots,T$, the learner selects $x^t \in \mathcal{X}$ and observes $f^t(x^t) = f^*(x^t) + \varepsilon^t$, where $f^*:\mathbb{Z}^\V\to[0, 1] \cup \set{-\infty}$ is an unknown M${}^{\natural}$-concave function and $(\varepsilon^t)_{t=1}^T$ is a sequence of i.i.d.\ $1$-sub-Gaussian noises

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic bandit M-natural-concave function maximization (cumulative regret)
unmapped: Unknown reward f* is an M-natural-concave function on the integer lattice Z^d with values in [0,1]; actions are integer vectors x in dom f* with x(V) <= m (not just subsets)
learner is told the feasible set via a poly(d)-time membership oracle
settings.definition_quote: the learner aims to minimize the expected cumulative regret (or the pseudo-regret, strictly speaking): \mathrm{Reg}_T \coloneqq T \cdot f^*(x^*) - \E\brc*{\sum_{t=1}^T f^*(x^t)}.

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial full-information online M-natural-concave function maximization (lower bound)
unmapped: Reward functions f^t are M-natural-concave (gross substitute) set functions on {0,1}^d with values in [0,1]
full information is given as free access to a poly(d)-time value oracle of f^t
settings.definition_quote: An oblivious adversary chooses an arbitrary sequence of M${}^\natural$-concave functions, $f^1,\dots,f^T$, where $f^t:\mathbb{Z}^\V\to[0, 1] \cup \set{-\infty}$ ... the learner selects $x^t \in \mathcal{X}$ and observes $f^t$, i.e., full-information feedback. ... we focus on the case where the constraint is specified by $K = N$ and $f^1,\dots,f^T$ are defined on $\set*{0, 1}^\V$

algorithms.name: Greedy with MOSS-based pure exploration per step (Algorithm 1 + MOSS)
Explore-then-commit with greedy MOSS simple-regret algorithm

conditions: 0 in dom f* and dom f* subset of Z_{>=0}^N
tuning: each of K phases runs MOSS for floor(T/K) rounds and outputs an arm sampled from the empirical play distribution

source.label: thm:simple-regret
source.quote: There is an algorithm that makes up to $T$ queries to the noisy value oracle of $f^*$ and outputs $x^{T+1}$ such that $\mathrm{sReg}_T = O(K^{3/2}\sqrt{N/T})$.

results.notes: Paper's N (ground-set size / lattice dimension) mapped to d, and its cardinality constraint K mapped to m. Polynomial time is implied: K runs of MOSS with at most N+1 arms.

conditions: 0 in dom f* and dom f* subset of Z_{>=0}^N
tuning: exploration length tilde T = Theta(K N^{1/3} T^{2/3})

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: There is an algorithm that achieves $\mathrm{Reg}_T = O(KN^{1/3}T^{2/3})$.

results.notes: The paper defines Reg_T through f*, so it is pseudo-regret. N mapped to d and K mapped to m.

symbols.c_exp: any constant c > 0 in the excluded regret rate poly(N) T^{1-c}

conditions: polynomial-time randomized learner (poly(N,T) time per round for every realization of randomness)
K = N and functions defined on {0,1}^N
computational hardness via reduction from 3-matroid intersection (oracle query lower bound)

source.label: thm:hardness
source.quote: In the adversarial full-information setting, for any constant $c>0$, no polynomial-time randomized learner can achieve a regret upper bound of $\mathrm{poly}(N)\cdot T^{1-c}$ in expectation.

results.notes: This is a computational hardness result, not an information-theoretic one: a learner taking exponential time per round (multiplicative weights over 2^N experts) achieves poly(N) sqrt(T). The schema has no clean encoding, so the result is recorded as: no poly(N) T^{1-c} upper bound exists for poly-time learners.
